shap_explain_tabular_sample#

class imbal.classification.shap_explain_tabular_sample(sample, model, training_data, class_names=None, feature_names=None, actual_label=None, label_to_explain=None, plot_type='bar', show=True, figure_save_path='shap-explanation.png', save_figure=False)#

Bases:

Utilizes kernel SHAP to generate an explanation for the classification of a particular sample by a given model. For more about SHAP, see this page.

Parameters:

  • sample – The sample to generate a SHAP explanation for.

  • model – The PyTorch model to generate a SHAP explanation from.

  • training_data – A Numpy array containing the data the given model was trained on.

  • class_names – Optional, default None. An array of strings, which maps class labels (as integer indices) to class names. Used to label the generated figure.

  • feature_names – Optional, default None. An array of strings, which maps features (by integer index) to feature names. Used to label the generated figure.

  • actual_label – Optional, default None. The actual label for the sample being explained. Used to label the generated figure.

  • label_to_explain – Optional, default None. The label of the class you wish to generate an explanation for. This label need not be the same as the true label for the provided image. When set to None, the label that is predicted by the model will be explained.

  • plot_type – Optional, default "bar". The type of plot to generate. Available options are "bar" and "waterfall". See SHAP documentation.

  • show – Optional, default True. Whether to show the generated figure. If set to False, the figure can be further modified before displaying or saving it.

  • save_figure – Optional, default False. Whether to save the generated figure.

  • figure_save_path – Optional, default "shap-explanation.png". The path to save the generated figure to.

Returns:

None

Example:

>>> # Assume a TensorFlow model is already saved to 'model'
>>>
>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
>>> 
>>> x, y = load_wine(return_X_y=True)
>>> labels = load_wine().feature_names
>>>
>>> imbal.classification.shap_explain_tabular_sample(
>>>     x[0],
>>>     model,
>>>     x_train,
>>>     plot_type='waterfall',
>>>     class_names=['Region 1', 'Region 2', 'Region 3'],
>>>     feature_names=labels
>>> )

Plot Examples#

Below is an example of the waterfall plot for a correctly predicted sample in the scikit-learn wine dataset.

>>> imbal.classification.shap_explain_tabular_sample(
>>>     x,
>>>     model,
>>>     x_train,
>>>     class_names=['Region 1', 'Region 2', 'Region 3'],
>>>     feature_names=labels,
>>>     plot_type='waterfall'
>>> )

Below is an example of the bar plot for an incorrectly predicted sample.

>>> imbal.classification.shap_explain_tabular_sample(
>>>     x,
>>>     model,
>>>     x_train,
>>>     class_names=['Region 1', 'Region 2', 'Region 3'],
>>>     feature_names=labels,
>>>     plot_type='bar'
>>> )

Below is an example of a bar plot explanation of the correct class for the incorrectly predicted sample shown above.

>>> imbal.classification.shap_explain_tabular_sample(
>>>     x,
>>>     model,
>>>     x_train,
>>>     label_to_explain=y,
>>>     class_names=['Region 1', 'Region 2', 'Region 3'],
>>>     feature_names=labels,
>>>     plot_type='bar'
>>> )
